newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Upward momentum building up in T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Upward momentum building up in T-bonds.

text.p: Upward momentum was building up in U.S. Treasury bond futures after Tuesday's sharp rally, technical analysts said.
The June T-bond contract was up about half a point in the mid-109 area in late morning trade, bouncing back from an early half-point loss.

The weekly stochastic tentatively upcrossed on Tuesday's rally, although the percent-K and D values at the end of this Friday, when the weekly will be formally memorialized, probably will not show an upcross, said Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage.
"The die is cast," he said. "Even though it's going to miss the cross on Friday, it's so close now that one of these Fridays in the next couple of months it's going to make it."
He added that the monthly stochastic, whose negative K/D spread was gradually narrowing, was also likely to upcross in the coming months.
"My theory...is don't fight the weekly and don't fight the monthly," he said.
In the very near term, however, Grauer said the up-cycle in the daily stochastic was near exhaustion and intraday stochastics like the 60- and 100-minute were overbought.

He expected a pullback of about two points, similar to the slide after a sharp bounce from lows of last June. He noted that Tuesday's two-point rally following a series of bullish divergences in the daily stochastic in recent weeks was nearly identical to last June's basing pattern.

Terence Gabriel, a technical analyst with I.D.E.A. Inc, also said stochastics and other oscillators were picking up and noted that Tuesday's rally pushed June T-bonds above the upper boundary of the daily Bollinger band. A Bollinger band consists of a moving average plus and minus a standard deviation.
"We broke out above the upper Bollinger band with a strong close, and we have a band-width expansion," he said. "It suggests that we do have sustainable trend momentum here."

Still, Gabriel urged caution in the near term as 109-28/32, the descending four-by-one Gann line from the September 1993 highs, and 110-00, the 200-day moving average, form a significant resistance area.
He said he would recommend new longs after the June contract cleared 110-10/32. From there, the target would be a trendline drawn from the December 1996 highs, now coming in at around 111-20/32.
A pullback below 108 would suggest that the recent upmove was a false breakout and that the market could return to the 107-108 range trading, Gabriel added.

In Eurodollar futures, Gabriel said the September contract vaulted past various resistance levels in Tuesday's rally. He said the upmove could also be seen as a bounce from a two-by-one ascending Gann line from the July 1996 lows.
The contract, virtually unchanged today from Tuesday's 93.875 close, would likely test the 200-day moving average at 93.94 in the near term, Gabriel said.
